Helena — thanks for the clear list. Summary below and attaching our standard DPA + current subprocessors export. Short answers first: SCCs: yes (we use EU SCCs); Dedicated: Redwood-managed infra uses a small set of third-party providers but we can agree operational guardrails; Private/VPC: controls available to keep data inside your network and optional on-prem eliminates cross-border transfer.

High-level:
- Subprocessors: core cloud infra (GCP/Azure/AWS), monitoring (Datadog/Prometheus), CDNs for model assets. Full list attached (subprocessors_list_20260218.csv).
- Dedicated: by default customer content is processed by Redwood runtime and the above subprocessors. We are open to a clause that requires customer consent before adding new subprocessors that will process content in Dedicated pools.
- VPC/Private: customer-managed network and optional on-prem remove most third-party access; support and control-plane access can be limited via role-based access and KMS integrations.
- SCCs & transfers: we offer SCCs for EU transfers and document that in our DPA.
- SOC 2: we can provide a rolling SOC 2 Type II report and an SOC carve-out for dedicated deployments (redacted where necessary).

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v1_20260218.pdf (standard DPA), subprocessors_list_20260218.csv

Process: if you want to redline, send to procurement/legal and we can coordinate with our counsel. We support DocuSign and AdobeSign; whichever you prefer is fine.

Thanks Sergio — forwarding our standard procurement redlines for DPAs so you have visibility. Our legal team prefers the following changes:

1) Limitation on subprocessors that will process customer content, especially for Dedicated pools — prefer only named providers.
2) Retention: logs used for debugging must be retained no more than 12 months and must be deletable on request.
3) Audit evidence: SOC 2 + management response to any exceptions.
4) For EU customers: require SCCs and a clause that data will not be moved outside the EU absent written consent.

See attached Procureco_DPA_Redlines.docx — that should give your legal a good place to start.

Subject: Redwood DPA - proposed redline summary

Helena / Sergio — attaching a short redline summary from our counsel after reviewing ProcureCo's doc. Key changes we propose and rationale:

- Subprocessors (Section 3): we propose a dual-track approach:
  * Dedicated (Reserved capacity): Redwood will list named subprocessors and will not engage additional subprocessors to process customer content in a given Dedicated pool without 30 days' notice and prior customer consent.
  * Private/VPC and On-Prem: when deployed in a customer-managed VPC or on-premises, Redwood's reliance on subprocessors is limited to offer/support functions we can scope; we can add a clause stating that customer data is only accessible per the specific config (i.e., support tunnelling requires explicit customer authorization).
- EU transfers (Section 7): we will accept SCCs and include them as an annex; for EU accounts, we can add a 'data residency' obligation to restrict exports without written consent.
- Logging/Retention: propose 12 months default for support/debug logs and a deletion mechanism on request (subject to lawful hold).
- Evidence: we will provide SOC 2 Type II and can provide redacted copies for procurement review.

I've attached DPA_redline_summary_20260220.pdf which highlights the proposed language. If these items look OK to TrustCorp, we can prepare an integrated redline and circulate for signature (DocuSign).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Helena — thanks, and appreciate the clarity. Confirmations and next steps below:

1) Subprocessors that may process customer content in Dedicated:
   - Cloud providers (AWS, GCP) — compute only; access governed by contract and RBAC.
   - Storage layer for model artifacts (S3, GCS) — only for persisted artifacts; we can limit caching to regional buckets.
   - Monitoring/ops: Datadog (metrics), Sentry (errors) — these receive telemetry and anonymized traces by default; we can disable error telemetry that contains user content by config for Dedicated pools.
   - Note: Redwood will not engage any new subprocessors to process customer content in a named Dedicated pool without 30 days' notice and your consent per the proposed clause.

2) VPC/Private/on-prem:
   - VPC: data flows stay within your cloud account/region; control plane calls are minimised and require explicit role-based access.
   - Private (on-prem): no third-party processing — model inference happens entirely in-customer environment unless customer opts in for managed backups.

3) SCCs & Data Residency:
   - We will attach EU SCCs as an annex for EU customers and add a data residency restriction for EU accounts preventing export without written consent.

4) Retention & audit: 12 months default for debugging logs, deletion-on-request workflow (we'll provide an API and process; exceptions for legal hold). SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA.

5) Execution: I've uploaded the final integrated DPA and triggered DocuSign for an authorized Redwood signatory. DocuSign completion URL: https://docusign.com/complete?doc=REDWOOD-DPA-20260224
   - Receipt attached: executed_dpa_docusign_receipt.pdf (stub).

If everything reads OK to TrustCorp, procurement can countersign and we'll start onboarding. Jumping Neha in to schedule a short technical call for Dedicated pool sizing and key management options.

Best regards,
Sergio Alvarez
